S015-01.notes: Seven volumes recording nearly every letter/rehearsal/illness = exhaustive. Laconic/perfunctory are opposites; tendentious unsupported.

S015-02.notes: Appositive 'a strange exception' defines anomaly directly. All four options take 'an', so the article gives no clue.

flags: minor: C is the only choice expressing counts rather than percentages, which makes it stand out to test-wise students
S015-03.notes: Claim is about number surviving per m2 rising; requires density x rate: 10x0.9=9, 80x0.4=32. A/B/D cite only rates. Data internally consistent (9, 15, 22, 32 rising).

S015-04.notes: If predation constrains brightness, removing predators predicts brighter males. B contradicts the premise; C is the null result; A irrelevant/opposite.

S015-05.notes: Singular gerund subject 'Restoring' (intervening plural 'mills'/'canals' are traps) needs singular finite verb; 'took' also parallels 'cost'. A/B plural, C non-finite fragment.

S015-06.notes: Nonessential participial phrase is closed by the comma after 'Rashid', so it must open with a comma. A leaves a lone comma; C 'which rediscovered' makes the stone the agent (illogical) ; D semicolon creates fragment.

flags: minor: 'Therefore' is a tempting distractor (fast growth -> harvestable), though survival after harvest is from regrowth, not a consequence of fast growth
S015-07.notes: Second sentence adds another advantage of bamboo; additive transition Moreover.

flags: minor: C is partially defensible (names Varga and the work) but does not tell an unfamiliar audience who Varga is; D is the standard 'introduce work and creator' answer
S015-08.notes: Goal requires introducing the mural while identifying Varga for unfamiliar readers; D gives her identity plus the work's size, subject, date. A omits Varga; B omits the mural; C presumes familiarity with Varga.

S015-09.notes: Text: bedrock rising faster than assumed, may help slow retreat. A contradicts 'assumed slowly'; B unsupported; D overstates ('soon', 'entirely').

flags: minor: same skill/structure as S015-03 within one batch (table-compute-the-difference item); passage_id 000129 is out of sequence with the rest of the batch (000137-000145)
S015-10.notes: Rural gap 73-64=9 vs urban 75-72=3. Only A compares the gaps; B/C/D true but don't address the size of the advantage.
